title: Issuing employee stock options (ESOP) in an unlisted company
law: Section 62(1)(b); Rule 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014
summary: Lets an unlisted company give employees the option to buy its shares later at a fixed price, through an approved scheme.
when: When an unlisted company wants to reward or retain employees and directors with options over its shares.
applies: Unlisted companies (listed companies follow the SEBI share based employee benefits rules)

steps.d: Work with management on who is eligible, the maximum number of options (the pool), the vesting period and conditions, and the exercise price and exercise period. Check that each class of person qualifies as an 'employee' under Rule 12.
Approve the scheme, authorise a compensation committee, and call a general meeting to pass a special resolution under Section 62(1)(b). Approve the notice and the explanatory statement.

Hold the general meeting. The explanatory statement must carry the disclosures listed in Rule 12(2). Pass a separate resolution if you will grant to employees of a subsidiary or holding company, or grant to identified employees 1% or more of issued capital in a year.
File the special resolution with the Registrar.
Hold a board meeting to form the compensation committee (for unlisted public companies, the nomination and remuneration committee).

The committee, or the board if there is no committee, grants options to eligible employees. Send each employee a grant letter stating the number of options, the vesting schedule and the exercise price.
Options vest as the scheme says. At least one year must pass between the grant and the vesting.

On vesting, the employee pays the exercise price and exercises the option. Get a valuation report to fix the perquisite value, and make sure perquisite tax is paid on the employee's behalf where the scheme requires.
Hold a board meeting or pass a circular resolution to allot the shares, in demat or physical form.
File the return of allotment and update the register of members.
Keep the Register of Employee Stock Options at the registered office. Give the Rule 12(9) details of the scheme in the directors' report.

The company sets any lock-in on shares. Option holders get no dividend or vote until shares are issued. Options cannot be transferred, pledged or encumbered, and only the employee can exercise them (a legal heir may, on death).

forms.purpose: Filing of special resolution approving the scheme
forms.deadline: Within 30 days of passing the resolution

forms.purpose: Return of allotment
Register of employee stock options (a register, not a filing)

checklist: Articles permit the issue of options
Employee eligibility checked against Rule 12 (promoters and 10% holders excluded)
ESOP scheme drafted and approved by the board
Special resolution passed and MGT-14 filed

resolutions.title: Approval of ESOP scheme and calling the general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the members, the Employee Stock Option Scheme [name of scheme] (the Scheme), placed before the meeting, be and is hereby approved for the grant of up to [number] options to eligible employees and directors of {co}, under Section 62(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and that the notice and explanatory statement placed before the meeting be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to sign the notice and file the required forms.

resolutions.title: Approval of the ESOP scheme
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 62(1)(b) and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, the [name of scheme] (the Scheme) be and is hereby approved, and the Board or the compensation committee be authorised to grant up to [number] options, each exercisable for one equity share of Rs. [face value] of {co}, to the eligible employees. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution, including settling any question about the Scheme.
resolutions.explanatory: The Scheme is placed before members for approval under Section 62(1)(b). Details under Rule 12(2): (a) total number of options to be granted: [number]; (b) identification of classes of employees entitled: [classes]; (c) requirements of vesting and the period of vesting: [details, minimum one year]; (d) maximum period within which options will vest: [period]; (e) exercise price or pricing formula: [details]; (f) exercise period and process of exercise: [details]; (g) lock-in period, if any: [details]; (h) maximum number of options granted per employee and in aggregate: [number]; (i) method used to value the options: [method]; (j) the conditions under which options lapse on termination of employment: [details]. None of the directors or key managerial personnel, except to the extent of options that may be granted to them, is interested in this resolution.

resolutions.title: Grant of options to employees of subsidiary or holding company and to identified employees
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 62(1)(b) of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 12 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, approval be and is hereby given to grant options under the Scheme to the employees of [subsidiary / holding company], and to identified employees in any one year equal to or exceeding one per cent of the issued capital of {co}, as the Board or the compensation committee may decide. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to take all steps to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Under Rule 12(1) a separate resolution is needed for grants to employees of a subsidiary or holding company, and for grants in one year to identified employees equal to or exceeding 1% of issued capital. The same disclosures as in Item 2 apply.

resolutions.title: Constitution of compensation committee
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT a Compensation Committee of the Board be constituted, consisting of [names of directors], to administer the Scheme of {co}. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Committee be authorised to grant options to eligible employees, and to decide vesting, exercise and all other matters under the Scheme, on the terms approved by the members.

resolutions.title: Grant of stock options
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT in terms of the Scheme approved by the members on [date], [number] options be and are hereby granted to the employees listed in the schedule placed before the meeting, at an exercise price of Rs. [amount] per option and subject to vesting after [period, not less than one year] from the date of grant. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to issue grant letters to the employees concerned.

resolutions.title: Allotment of shares on exercise of options
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each be and are hereby allotted to the option holders listed in the schedule placed before the meeting, who have exercised their options under the Scheme and paid Rs. [amount] per share. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the names of the allottees be entered in the register of members, share certificates be issued or the shares be credited to their demat accounts, and the return of allotment be filed with the Registrar within the time allowed.

docs.title: Grant letter to employee
paras: Dear [name of employee], {co} is pleased to grant you [number] stock options under the [name of scheme] on [date of grant].

Each option entitles you to subscribe to one equity share of Rs. [face value] at an exercise price of Rs. [amount]. The options will vest as follows: [vesting schedule, with at least one year between grant and first vesting]. You may exercise vested options within [exercise period].

Options cannot be transferred, pledged or otherwise encumbered. You will have no right to dividend or vote until shares are allotted to you on exercise. Please sign and return the copy of this letter as acceptance. For {co}: [name], [designation].

flags: The reference note says a private company may pass an ordinary resolution instead of a special resolution, and need not file MGT-14. Section 62(1)(b) requires a special resolution for every company that issues ESOPs, private companies included. Please confirm the current rule before relying on that point.

The reference note calls the committee a compensation committee. Rule 12 refers to the nomination and remuneration committee for companies that must have one; a private company without one may let the board grant options. Check the current Rule 12 wording.

The reference note says an ordinary resolution is enough for grants to subsidiary or holding company employees and for 1% or more to identified employees. Rule 12(1) calls for a separate resolution (and Section 62(1)(b) needs a special one). Treat as special unless you confirm otherwise.
The Rule 12 definition quoted in the reference note has bracketed amendment notes; confirm the current text, including the ten-year start-up exemption, on the MCA site.
private: A private company may approve a Section 62(1)(b) issue by ordinary resolution, not special, but it must then file Form MGT-14. A compensation committee is optional for a private company, while an unlisted public company must have a Nomination and Remuneration Committee that approves the grants.

title: Issuing sweat equity shares
law: Sections 2(88), 39, 54, 96, 100, 173; Rule 8 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Rule 12 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014; SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 and SEBI LODR Regulations 30 and 46(3) for listed companies
summary: Lets a company issue equity shares at a discount, or for non-cash value such as know-how or intellectual property, to directors and employees.
when: When a company wants to reward directors or employees for know-how, intellectual property or value addition by issuing shares.
applies: Private, public and listed companies (extra SEBI rules for listed)

steps.d: Confirm that the articles allow sweat equity shares. If not, alter them by special resolution. Check that each recipient is an eligible employee or director. Listed companies must also check the SEBI regulations and LODR.
A permanent employee who has worked in or outside India for at least one year, a director (whole-time or not), or an employee or director of a holding or subsidiary company.
A registered valuer values the shares and the know-how, intellectual property or value addition received. The reference note also names a merchant banker for valuing the know-how; see flags.
Consider the proposal, approve the notice of the general meeting, fix its date, time and venue, and approve the explanatory statement with all disclosures.

Include: date of the board approval; why the issue is made; class and total number of shares; classes of recipients; terms and valuation basis; period of association; names and relationship with promoters or key managerial personnel; issue price; consideration including non-cash; effect on managerial remuneration limits; accounting treatment; and diluted EPS after the issue.
Pass a special resolution under Section 54. The allotment must be made within 12 months of the resolution.
File the special resolution with the Registrar.
Approve the allotment to the named employees or directors. A secretarial auditor's certificate that the issue follows the law and the resolution is to be placed before the members.
File the return of allotment.
steps.time: The reference note says within 15 days; see flags

steps.d: Issue share certificates to the allottees.
Enter the shares in the register of members and in the Register of Sweat Equity Shares.
Follow the SEBI regulations, tell the stock exchanges under LODR Regulation 30, and post the information on the website under Regulation 46(3).
Apply the correct accounting standard (Ind AS 102 for share based payments) and give the details in the board's report under Section 134(3).

forms.purpose: Filing of special resolution
Return of allotment
forms.deadline: The reference note says 15 days; Rule 12 of the PAS Rules and Section 39(4) give 30 days

forms.purpose: Register of sweat equity shares (a register)

checklist: Recipients are eligible under Section 2(88) and Rule 8
Board approval of notice and explanatory statement
Allotment made within 12 months of resolution
Register of sweat equity shares updated
Listed company: SEBI and LODR filings

meetings.notice_days: At least 21 clear days (shorter if 95% of members agree)

meetings.title: Board meeting to allot sweat equity shares

resolutions.title: Proposal to issue sweat equity shares and calling the general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the members, the issue of up to [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each of {co} as sweat equity shares to [names or class of directors / employees], for [know-how / intellectual property / value addition], at Rs. [price] per share, as valued by the registered valuer, be and is hereby approved under Section 54 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 8 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue], and the notice and explanatory statement placed before the meeting be approved.

resolutions.title: Issue of sweat equity shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 54 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 8 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, consent be and is hereby given to issue up to [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each of {co} as sweat equity shares at Rs. [price] per share to [names or class of directors / employees], for consideration of [know-how / intellectual property / value addition], valued at Rs. [amount]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the shares will carry a lock-in as the Act and the rules require, and rank equally with existing equity shares after the lock-in. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the shares be allotted within twelve months from the date of this resolution and the Board be authorised to do all acts to give effect to it.
resolutions.explanatory: (a) Date of board meeting approving the proposal: [date]. (b) Reason for the issue: [reason]. (c) Class of shares: equity. (d) Total number of shares: [number]. (e) Class of directors or employees to receive them: [class]. (f) Terms and conditions, including the basis of valuation: [details]. (g) Period of association with the company: [period]. (h) Names of recipients and relationship with promoters or key managerial personnel: [details]. (i) Issue price: Rs. [price]. (j) Consideration, including non-cash: [details]. (k) Effect on the ceiling on managerial remuneration, and how it will be handled: [details]. (l) Accounting treatment: [standard]. (m) Diluted earnings per share after the issue: [amount]. None of the directors or key managerial personnel, except those named as recipients, is interested in this resolution.

resolutions.title: Alteration of articles to permit sweat equity shares (only if the articles do not allow them)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the articles of association of {co} be altered by inserting a new Article [number] allowing the company to issue sweat equity shares in accordance with Section 54 of the Act and the rules. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to file the resolution and altered articles with the Registrar.
resolutions.explanatory: The articles of the company do not now allow sweat equity shares. The alteration is needed before the issue in Item [number] can be made. None of the directors is interested except as a possible recipient.

resolutions.title: Allotment of sweat equity shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the special resolution passed on [date], [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, issued as sweat equity at Rs. [price], be and are hereby allotted to the persons listed in the schedule placed before the meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the names be entered in the register of members and the Register of Sweat Equity Shares, share certificates be issued within two months of allotment, and the return of allotment be filed with the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to sign all documents and forms.

flags: Return of allotment in Form PAS-3 is due within 30 days of allotment (Section 39(4) and Rule 12 of the PAS Rules). The reference note says 15 days in this procedure. Please confirm.

The reference note gives the lock-in as six months from the date of trading approval. Section 54 and Rule 8 provide a lock-in of three years from allotment for sweat equity shares of all companies. Listed companies must also check the SEBI regulations. Please verify.

The annual cap in the reference note is 15% of paid-up equity capital. Rule 8 says 15% or Rs. 5 crore in value, whichever is higher, with a 25% cap overall, and a higher limit for start-ups. Please confirm.
The reference note asks for valuation by a merchant banker. Rule 8 calls for a valuation by a registered valuer for the non-cash consideration. Please verify.
Section 54 allows sweat equity only for a class of shares already issued for at least one year. The reference note does not say so. Check.
The register of members is kept in Form MGT-1; the reference note says SH-3 for both. SH-3 is the Register of Sweat Equity Shares.
Share certificates must be signed by two directors (one a managing or whole-time director, if any) and the company secretary, if any. Check against Section 46 and the Rules.

The reference note lists Sections 39, 96 and 100 as governing provisions; only 39 (allotment) and 96/100 (meetings) are indirectly relevant. The secretarial auditor's certificate applies to listed companies under the rules. Check whether a private company needs it.
private: A private company is outside the SEBI rules. Only Section 54 and the Companies Rules apply, with no stock exchange intimation or website disclosure.

title: Issuing preference shares
law: Section 55; Rule 9 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014
summary: Sets out how a company issues redeemable preference shares, from the board decision to share certificates, and what to check before redeeming them.
when: When a company wants to raise funds by issuing preference shares.
applies: All companies (listed companies must also follow the SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018)

steps.d: Check that the articles allow preference shares (if not, alter them by special resolution). Only redeemable preference shares are allowed. The company must have no default in redeeming earlier preference shares or paying their dividend. The term must not exceed 20 years (30 years for infrastructure projects). Listed companies follow SEBI ICDR.
Send notice of the board meeting and complete the prior compliance.

Approve the proposal, fix the date, time and venue of the general meeting, approve the notice with the Section 102 and Rule 9(3) explanatory statement, authorise valuation and due diligence if needed, and authorise a director or the company secretary to sign documents and forms.
Get a registered valuer's report if the shares are issued at a premium or discount.
Send the notice with the explanatory statement under Section 102 and Rule 9(3).
Pass a special resolution to authorise the issue and the terms under Rule 9(2), and to authorise signatories.
File the special resolution with the Registrar.
If the issue is by private placement, send the offer letter to identified persons and keep a record of the offers.
File the offer letter and the resolution within 30 days.
For private placement, open a separate bank account to receive application money.
Accept money only through banking channels. No cash.
Send notice, then approve the allotment and the issue of share certificates, and authorise signatories.
File the return of allotment.
steps.time: The reference note says within 15 days; see flags

steps.d: Issue certificates with the required signatures.
Enter the allottees in the register of members under Section 88, and keep the preference shareholders' register up to date.
When redeeming, follow Section 55(2) and Rule 9(6).

Private placement offer letter

Return of allotment

checklist: Shares are redeemable, term 20 years or less (30 for infrastructure)
No existing default in redemption or dividend
Valuation report if premium or discount

resolutions.title: Approval of issue of preference shares and calling the general meeting
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the approval of the members, the issue of up to [number] [cumulative / non-cumulative] redeemable preference shares of Rs. [face value] each of {co}, at [par / a premium of Rs. ___], redeemable after [period, not more than 20 years], carrying dividend of [rate] per cent, under Section 55 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 9 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, be and is hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT a general meeting be held on [date] at [time] at [venue] and the notice and explanatory statement placed before the meeting be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to sign documents and forms.

resolutions.title: Issue of redeemable preference shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 55 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 9 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014, approval be and is hereby given to issue up to [number] redeemable preference shares of Rs. [face value] each of {co}, to [name of allottees / class], at [price], on the terms set out in the explanatory statement. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board and [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to do all acts and sign all documents and forms to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: The company proposes to raise Rs. [amount] by issuing redeemable preference shares. Particulars under Rule 9: (a) size and nature of the issue: [details]; (b) objects: [purpose]; (c) manner of issue (public / private placement): [details]; (d) price and basis of fixing it: [details]; (e) dividend rate and whether cumulative: [details]; (f) redemption period, not more than 20 years (30 for infrastructure): [period]; (g) redemption terms, including any premium: [details]; (h) any other rights attached: [details]. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except [names, if any].

resolutions.title: Alteration of articles to permit preference shares (only if needed)
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 14 of the Companies Act, 2013, the articles of association of {co} be altered by inserting Article [number] allowing the company to issue preference shares in accordance with Section 55 of the Act. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to file the resolution with the Registrar.
resolutions.explanatory: The articles do not now provide for preference shares. The alteration is needed before the issue in Item [number] is made. No director is interested.

resolutions.title: Allotment of preference shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT [number] redeemable preference shares of Rs. [face value] each of {co} be and are hereby allotted to the applicants listed in the schedule placed before the meeting, against receipt of Rs. [amount] through banking channels. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT share certificates be issued within two months of allotment under the signatures required by law, and the return of allotment be filed with the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to sign all documents and forms.

flags: Return of allotment in PAS-3 is due within 30 days of allotment (Section 39(4); Rule 12 of the PAS Rules). The reference note says 15 days. Please verify.

The reference note mentions a valuation if shares are issued at a discount. A company cannot issue shares at a discount except sweat equity (Section 53). Treat the valuation as relevant to a premium only.

The reference note says no part of this applies differently to private companies. A private company's exemptions under MCA notifications (for example on filing MGT-14 for some resolutions) should be checked.

Share certificates are signed by two directors (one managing or whole-time, if any) and the company secretary, if any. The reference note says two directors or one director and the company secretary. Check against Section 46.
The register of preference shareholders: MGT-1 is the register of members under Section 88. Check whether a separate register is intended.
private: Every provision for issuing preference shares applies to a private company.

title: Issuing non-convertible debentures by a private company
law: Sections 2(30), 42, 71 and 180; Rule 14 of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014; Rule 18 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Rule 2(1)(c) of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules; Rule 9B of the PAS Rules
summary: Shows how a private company issues debentures by private placement without the money being counted as a deposit, including meetings, offer letter, allotment, trust deed and filings.
when: When a private company wants to raise money by issuing debentures to identified investors.
applies: Private companies (secured NCDs or unsecured compulsorily convertible debentures)

steps.d: If NCDs are neither secured nor listed on a recognised exchange, they count as deposits. So a private company should issue either secured NCDs or unsecured fully or compulsorily convertible debentures.

Check that the articles give the board power to issue debentures. Allotment must be in demat form for a company that is not a small company. Get a valuation report from a registered valuer. Fix maturity, interest and security. Open a separate bank account.
Cover face value and any premium (not below fair value in the valuation), interest rate and payment terms, security, maturity and redemption amount, and lock-in or put option.

Approve the issue by private placement, the draft PAS-4 and PAS-5, the bank account, the debenture trustee, the depository and registrar and transfer agent for demat, and take the valuation report on record.
Pass special resolutions: borrowing powers under Section 180(1)(c) if the limit is exceeded, the private placement, the PAS-4 offer and its circulation, and the debenture trustee.
steps.time: At least 21 days notice, or shorter with consent

steps.d: Open a separate account with a scheduled bank for the subscription money.
File the special resolution with the Registrar, attaching the offer letter, valuation report, certified true copy of the resolution, and the notice with explanatory statement.
Appoint the debenture trustee before the offer is made, if one is needed.
Send PAS-4 only after MGT-14 is filed. Offer to no more than 200 persons in a financial year. Send the offers within 30 days of identifying the persons.
Keep a complete record of the offers.
Investors pay only through banking channels into the separate account.

Coordinate with the depository and registrar for an ISIN and for corporate action after allotment. Documents: certificate of incorporation, PAN, memorandum, articles, board resolution, tripartite agreement.
Allot the debentures, agree to create a charge, approve issue of certificates and payment of stamp duty, and approve the trust deed.
steps.time: Allot within 60 days of receiving money

steps.d: File the return with a list of allottees (name, address, PAN, email, class, date, number and amount) and attach the board resolution, PAS-4, PAS-5 and the valuation report.
Execute the debenture trust deed.
Create the reserve and transfer the required amount.
If the debentures are secured, register the charge.
steps.time: Within 30 days of creation of charge

steps.d: Have the registrar credit the NCDs to investors' demat accounts with NSDL or CDSL, obtain the BENPOS statement and pay stamp duty.
Enter the holders in the register.
Submit the return to the Registrar.
steps.time: Within 60 days of end of each half year

resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Section 180(1)(c) of the Companies Act, 2013, the Board be and is hereby authorised to borrow money, including by issue of debentures, in excess of the aggregate of the paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium of {co}, up to Rs. [amount] at any time. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to create security over the assets of {co} for such borrowings.
resolutions.explanatory: The company needs funds of Rs. [amount] for [purpose]. The present borrowing limit of Rs. [amount] is not enough. The Board therefore seeks approval to borrow up to Rs. [amount]. No director or key managerial personnel is interested except to the extent of any debentures they may hold.

resolutions.title: Issue of debentures by private placement, offer letter and trustee
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT pursuant to Sections 42 and 71 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the relevant rules, approval be and is hereby given to issue up to [number] [secured non-convertible / unsecured compulsorily convertible] debentures of Rs. [face value] each, aggregating Rs. [amount], on private placement to identified persons on the terms in the offer letter in Form PAS-4. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to circulate the offer letter, appoint [name of trustee] as debenture trustee, and do all acts needed to give effect to this resolution.
resolutions.explanatory: Particulars: (a) object of the issue: [purpose]; (b) number and class of debentures: [details]; (c) price and basis of the price (see valuation report): [details]; (d) rate of interest and payment terms: [details]; (e) security: [details]; (f) maturity and redemption: [details]; (g) persons to whom offered: [details]. This approval may cover all offers made within one year. No director is interested except [names, if any].

resolutions.title: Allotment of debentures
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT [number] debentures of Rs. [face value] each be and are hereby allotted to the persons listed in the schedule placed before the meeting, against receipt of Rs. [amount] in the separate bank account. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment be made within sixty days of receipt of the application money and the return of allotment be filed with the Registrar.

resolutions.title: Creation of charge
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT {co} create a [first / pari passu] charge on [description of property] in favour of [name of trustee] for the debentures, and that [name of director] be authorised to sign the agreement, and to file the particulars of the charge with the Registrar.

resolutions.title: Issue of debenture certificates and payment of stamp duty
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the debentures be credited to the demat accounts of the allottees through the depository, or debenture certificates be issued under the signatures required by law, and stamp duty of Rs. [amount] be paid on the allotment as the law requires.

resolutions.title: Execution of trust deed
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the debenture trust deed between {co} and [name of trustee], placed before the meeting, be approved and be signed by [name of director] within sixty days of allotment.

docs.title: Key terms for the debenture subscription agreement
paras: This Agreement is made on [date] between {co} (the Company) and [name of investor] (the Investor).

The Company will issue [number] [secured non-convertible / unsecured compulsorily convertible] debentures of Rs. [face value] each at [par / premium of Rs. ___], which is not below the fair value of Rs. [amount] stated in the valuation report dated [date].

Interest will be paid at [rate] per cent per annum, payable [monthly / quarterly / annually]. The debentures will mature on [date] and will be redeemed at Rs. [amount]. Security: [description]. Other terms: [lock-in, put option, if any].

flags: The reference note says PAS-3 is due within 15 days of allotment. Section 39(4) and Rule 12 of the PAS Rules provide 30 days. Please verify.

The reference note says to credit the debenture redemption reserve with an amount equal to the debentures. Rule 18(7) generally needs 10% of the outstanding amount (and exempts some companies, such as listed companies, NBFCs and housing finance companies). Please check what applies to this issue.
The reference note says to enter debenture holders in MGT-1. MGT-1 is the register of members; the register of debenture holders is kept under Section 88 in Form MGT-2. Please verify.
PAS-6 (half-yearly reconciliation) applies under Rule 9A to unlisted public companies; check whether it applies to a private company after the Rule 9B changes.
The reference note cites Rule 2(1)(c) of the Deposits Rules for the secured-or-listed condition. Check the exact sub-clause that now exempts debentures, as it has been amended.
The 60-day deadline for the trust deed and the time to file the PAS-4 copy with the Registrar should be checked against Rule 18 and Rule 14.
Section 180(1)(c): check if the company needs this approval at all, and the exemption notified for private companies.

title: Transferring physical shares in a private company
law: Sections 2(68), 44, 56, 58 and 88; Secretarial Standard 1; Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
summary: Covers the transfer of shares held in paper form: the transfer form, stamp duty, board approval, registers, new certificates, and what to do if the company refuses.
when: When a shareholder of a private company sells or gifts shares held in physical form.

steps.d: A private company restricts the right to transfer its shares in its articles. Read the restrictions before going ahead.

Not required by the Act, but advisable to avoid tax issues and disputes. If a non-resident is a party, FEMA, the NDI Rules and RBI guidelines apply and fix the valuation. If a party is from a country sharing a land border with India, prior government approval is needed and goes with Form SH-4.
Not mandatory, but sensible. Set out the number and type of shares, price, mode and instalments of payment, timeline and date of transfer, and how disputes are handled.
Both parties sign Form SH-4 and pay stamp duty (at present 0.015% of the price) by share transfer stamps or franking. Check first whether certificates must be split.

Send the signed and stamped SH-4 with the share certificates (or the allotment letter if no certificate exists). The company verifies identities, stamping, the articles, the Act and other laws. If someone signs for a party, it checks the power of attorney or board resolution.
docs: Power of attorney or board resolution, if any

steps.d: Approve the transfer under Section 173 and SS-1. The board may also approve any share split, authorise a person to register the transfer, and, if the articles permit, delegate approval to a committee. For partly paid shares transferred on the transferor's application alone, send notice to the transferee; transfer is not registered if they object within 2 weeks.
docs: Notice to transferee for partly paid shares

steps.d: Enter the transfer in the register of members and the register of transfers, if kept.
Endorse or cancel the old certificate and issue a new certificate to the transferee.
Show the transfer in the annual return.
A private company may refuse to register a transfer. Send reasons to the transferor and transferee. The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal.
steps.time: Notice within 30 days of delivery of SH-4; appeal within 30 days of notice, or within 60 days of delivery if no notice is sent

steps.d: FEMA, the NDI Rules and RBI directions may apply. Usually Form FC-TRS goes to RBI, and later the company files the FLA return.
steps.time: FC-TRS within 60 days of transfer or receipt of funds, whichever is earlier

forms.purpose: Securities transfer form
forms.deadline: Deliver to the company within 60 days of execution

forms.purpose: Notice to transferee for partly paid shares
forms.deadline: On application by the transferor alone

forms.purpose: Register of members (a register)
Annual return (other than small companies and OPCs)
Annual return for small companies and OPCs
Reporting transfer involving non-resident
forms.deadline: Within 60 days of transfer or receipt of funds

checklist: Form SH-4 signed by both parties
Government approval if a land border country is involved
FC-TRS and FLA return if a non-resident is a party

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve share transfer
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the articles and Secretarial Standard 1 allow it)

resolutions.title: Approval of transfer of shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the transfer of [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, bearing distinctive numbers [from] to [to], held by [name of transferor] in {co} under certificate no. [number], to [name of transferee], as per the duly stamped Form SH-4 dated [date] received on [date], be and is hereby approved under Section 56 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the shares be split, if needed, and the transfer be entered in the register of members, and new share certificates be issued to the transferee within one month of receipt of the transfer form. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to do all things needed to give effect to this resolution.

docs.title: Notice of refusal to register a transfer
paras: To: [name of transferor] and [name of transferee]

{co} has received the instrument of transfer dated [date] for [number] shares, delivered on [date]. Under Section 58 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the articles of the company, the Board has refused to register the transfer for the following reasons: [reasons].
You may appeal to the National Company Law Tribunal within thirty days of receiving this notice. For {co}: [name], [designation], [date].

flags: Stamp duty rate: the reference note says 0.015% of the price. Please check the current Indian Stamp Act and state-wise rates before paying.
Register entries 'within seven days' of board approval: check against Rule 5 of the Management and Administration Rules and Section 88.
Under Section 58 the Tribunal appeal period and refusal notice period should be checked against the current text; the reference note mixes the transfer-form and transmission dates.
The booklet lists MGT-7 or MGT-7A; the company must show only the correct one for its type.
Check whether a delegation of approval to a committee is actually allowed by Section 56 and the articles.

title: Transmission of physical shares on a shareholder's death
summary: Explains how legal heirs or a nominee have shares of a deceased member registered in their names in a private company.
when: When a shareholder holding physical shares dies and the legal heirs or nominee ask the company to register the shares.

steps.d: The legal heirs or nominee apply to the company giving their names and addresses, the names and addresses of the other legal heirs, the shares held by the deceased with certificate numbers, and a statement if no probate or succession certificate has been applied for.
The applicant provides a notarised or original death certificate, as the company's policy asks. The company also checks the articles for any special procedure.
If the deceased left a will, ask for probate. If there is no will, ask for a succession certificate from the court.
Take an indemnity bond with surety on stamp paper of the proper value (the reference note gives Rs. 500 for Maharashtra).
Get a no objection certificate from other legal heirs if the shares go to one person or to selected heirs jointly.
Collect proof of identity and address of each applicant and signature verification from the bank.
Pass a resolution at a board meeting or by circulation to approve the transmission.
Issue or endorse share certificates in the names of the applicants.
Make entries in the statutory registers.

checklist: Application by legal heirs or nominee
Indemnity bond and surety on stamp paper

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve transmission of shares
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the articles and Secretarial Standard 1 allow it)

resolutions.title: Approval of transmission of shares
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT on the death of [name of deceased member], the [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, held under folio no. [number] and certificate no(s). [numbers], be and are hereby transmitted to [name(s) of legal heirs / nominee], on the basis of the application, [probate / succession certificate], indemnity bond and other documents placed before the Board, under Section 56 of the Companies Act, 2013. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the names be entered in the register of members, share certificates be issued or endorsed in their names, and [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to do all things needed.

docs.title: Application for transmission of shares
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}.

I, [name of applicant], of [address], am the [legal heir / nominee] of the late [name of deceased], who held [number] shares in {co} under folio no. [number], certificate no(s). [numbers]. The other legal heirs are [names and addresses]. I [have / have not] applied for a probate or succession certificate.

I request that the shares be transmitted in [my name / joint names]. I attach the death certificate, [probate / succession certificate], indemnity bond, NOC from other legal heirs, and proof of identity and address. Signed: [name], [date].

docs.title: Indemnity bond
paras: I, [name], of [address], in consideration of {co} registering the transmission of [number] shares of the late [name of deceased] in my name, hereby agree to indemnify {co} and its directors against any claim, loss or damage arising from the transmission.

I confirm that the information I have given is true, that I am the lawful claimant, and that no other person has a claim over the shares. Surety: [name and address]. Executed on stamp paper of Rs. [value] on [date].

flags: Stamp paper value (Rs. 500 for Maharashtra) varies by state and has changed over time. Check the current duty for your state.
The reference note gives no time limit. Section 56(4) requires certificates to be delivered within a set time after intimation of transmission; check the current limit.
Nomination under Section 72 can simplify transmission; the reference note does not mention it.

title: Issuing share certificates for an IEPF claim
law: Section 124; Rule 7 of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016
summary: Explains how a shareholder reclaims shares and dividend moved to the IEPF, and how the company handles a duplicate certificate when the original or proof of entitlement is lost.
when: When a shareholder whose shares or dividend went to the IEPF asks the company for help, and the original certificate has been lost.
applies: Mainly listed and public companies; SEBI advertisement rules do not apply to private companies

steps.d: Shares on which dividend stayed unpaid or unclaimed for seven years are moved to the IEPF. The shareholder must confirm this.

The shareholder claims the shares and dividend from the IEPF under Rule 7, with proof of entitlement. Proof can be an entitlement letter from the company, bonds, debentures, fixed deposit receipts, share certificate, interest warrant, dividend warrant or application number, or a statement of transaction or loss documents.
If the original certificate, bond, deposit receipt, debenture certificate or proof of entitlement is lost, the company and claimant follow the Share Capital Rules, SEBI LODR rules and circulars.
On a request for a duplicate certificate, check the supporting evidence and the indemnity bond.

Check for a self-attested copy of the FIR or police complaint (if market value is over Rs. 5 lakh), an indemnity bond on non-judicial stamp paper attested by a notary, saying the securities were not sold or encumbered, and a copy of a newspaper advertisement about the loss (if value is over Rs. 5,00,000).
If the documents suffice, pass a board resolution (at a meeting or by circulation) to issue the duplicate certificate.
The face must say 'duplicate issued in lieu of share certificate No. ____'. It is signed by the directors and authorised signatory; if there is a company secretary, by the CS and another director.
Make the entries in the register of renewed and duplicate certificates.
docs: Register of renewed and duplicate certificates

forms.purpose: Claim for refund of shares or dividend from the IEPF (filed by the shareholder)
Register of renewed and duplicate share certificates (a register)

checklist: Claimant's IEPF-5 and proof of entitlement
Indemnity bond on stamp paper, notarised
FIR copy if value is above Rs. 5 lakh
Newspaper advertisement if value is above Rs. 5,00,000
Certificate marked duplicate with the old number
Signed by CS and a director

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve issue of duplicate certificate
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the articles and Secretarial Standard 1 allow it)

resolutions.title: Issue of duplicate share certificate
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, on the request of [name of shareholder] and on the basis of the indemnity bond, [FIR / police complaint], advertisement and other documents placed before the Board, a duplicate share certificate for [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, folio no. [number], in lieu of certificate no. [number], be and is hereby approved under Section 46 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Rules. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the certificate be marked 'duplicate issued in lieu of share certificate No. [number]', be signed by [name of director] and [name of company secretary], and be entered in the Register of Renewed and Duplicate Share Certificates.

docs.title: Newspaper notice of loss of share certificate
paras: NOTICE is hereby given that the share certificate no. [number] for [number] equity shares of {co}, registered in the name of [name], folio no. [number], has been lost, and the holder has applied for a duplicate.
Any person with a claim should write to the company at [address] within [number] days. After that period a duplicate will be issued.

docs.title: Indemnity bond
paras: I, [name], of [address], hold [number] shares in {co}. The original certificate no. [number] is lost and I have not sold or encumbered those shares. I will indemnify {co} against any loss or claim arising from the duplicate certificate. Executed on stamp paper of Rs. [value], notarised, on [date].

flags: The reference note says the shareholder confirms the transfer to IEPF, but the usual route is that the claimant files IEPF-5 online and the company verifies the claim and reports to the IEPF Authority, with shares credited to a demat account. Please check Rule 7 for the full steps and time limits.
The reference note title says 'issue of share certificates', but the content is mainly the IEPF claim and duplicate certificates; the actual company role under Rule 7 is limited.
SH-2 is the register of renewed and duplicate certificates. Check the current wording of the rule.
The Rs. 5 lakh value test in the reference note should be checked against current SEBI circulars.
private: SEBI requirements such as the newspaper advertisement do not apply.

title: Issuing a duplicate share certificate
law: Section 46; Rule 6 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014; Section 447
summary: Covers the steps for replacing a share certificate that is lost, destroyed, defaced or mutilated.
when: When a shareholder reports that a certificate is lost, destroyed, defaced or mutilated.
applies: All companies (extra steps for listed companies)

steps.d: The shareholder writes to the company reporting the loss, destruction, defacement or mutilation.

The shareholder gives an FIR or police complaint (mandatory for loss), an indemnity bond on non-judicial stamp paper, an affidavit about the loss, the original certificate if it is only defaced or mutilated, a newspaper advertisement (listed or public companies) and anything else the articles ask for.
The company may freeze transfers of that certificate to stop illegal transfers.
Hold a board meeting with proper notice. Approve the duplicate certificate after checking the documents.
Issue it under the signatures of two directors, or a director and the company secretary if there is one, and the common seal if the company has one. Mark it 'DUPLICATE'.
steps.time: Within 45 days of the request (see flags)

steps.d: Make entries in the Register of Renewed and Duplicate Share Certificates and note it in the remarks column of the register of members.
docs: Register of renewed and duplicate certificates

steps.d: A listed company tells the stock exchange.

forms.purpose: Register of renewed and duplicate share certificates (a register)

checklist: Entry in SH-2 and register of members

meetings.title: Board meeting to approve duplicate share certificate
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the articles and Secretarial Standard 1 allow it)

resolutions.title: Issue of duplicate share certificate
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT, on the request of [name of shareholder] and after checking the FIR, indemnity bond, affidavit and other documents placed before the Board, a duplicate share certificate for [number] equity shares of Rs. [face value] each, folio no. [number], in place of certificate no. [number], be and is hereby issued under Section 46 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Rule 6 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the certificate be marked 'DUPLICATE', signed by two directors, or by one director and the company secretary, and entered in the Register of Renewed and Duplicate Share Certificates.

docs.title: Affidavit of loss of share certificate
paras: I, [name], son or daughter of [name], resident of [address], state on oath that I hold [number] shares in {co}, folio no. [number], certificate no. [number], and that the original certificate has been [lost / destroyed] and has not been sold, pledged or transferred.
I request {co} to issue a duplicate certificate and I will indemnify {co} against any claim arising from it. Signed: [name], [date]. Sworn before me: [notary].

flags: The 45-day limit for duplicates: for listed companies SEBI LODR and its circulars give a shorter period (30 days) for service requests; Rule 6 allows unlisted companies three months. Please verify.
The reference note says to freeze transfers for 30 days. That is practice, not a statutory step.
The 24-hour intimation for listed companies should be checked against the current LODR provision.
Section 447 applies to fraud; it is not a step of the procedure.
private: A private company need not advertise in a newspaper unless the Articles say so. There is no stock exchange intimation (listed companies only). It may work without a common seal. An unlisted company has more time to issue a duplicate certificate, up to 3 months, against the 45 days for public and listed companies.

title: Filing the return for money received that is not a deposit
law: Rules 16 and 16A of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014; Rule 2(1)(c) of the same Rules
summary: Walks through preparing and filing Form DPT-3 to report outstanding money received that the rules do not treat as a deposit.
when: When a company has outstanding receipts, loans or amounts that are excluded from the definition of deposit and must be reported.

steps.d: Prepare a statement of outstanding amounts and sort it into categories such as secured and unsecured loans.
If applicable, get the statutory auditor to certify the nature of each receipt and that it complies with Rule 2(1)(c).
Hold a board meeting or pass a circular resolution to approve the statement of outstanding amounts (advisable) and authorise a director or the company secretary to file DPT-3.

steps.t: Log in to the MCA portal
steps.d: Use MCA V3: log in, go to MCA Services, Company e-filing, then Foreign Company, Deposits, Nidhi Company, and choose Form DPT-3 Return of Deposits.
Enter the CIN, the purpose of the form, the company's object and other details.
Attach the auditor's certificate, if applicable, the list of lenders with amounts, and the board resolution (optional).
Affix the digital signature of a director, manager, company secretary or other authorised person.
Upload the form and pay the fee, which depends on the company's nominal share capital.
Keep the MCA challan and SRN acknowledgement, auditor's certificate, board resolution and loan or advance agreements for inspection.

forms.purpose: Return of deposits and of particulars of transactions not considered as deposits
forms.deadline: Check the due date in Rule 16 and 16A (usually by 30 June for the year ended 31 March)

checklist: Statement of outstanding amounts as on 31 March

meetings.title: Circular resolution to approve the DPT-3 statement and filing
meetings.notice_days: Draft sent to all directors

resolutions.title: Approval of statement of outstanding amounts and filing of DPT-3
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the statement of outstanding receipts of money or loans not treated as deposits as on [31 March year], placed before the Board, be and is hereby approved under Rules 16 and 16A of the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to sign and file Form DPT-3 with the Registrar, attaching the auditor's certificate, if applicable, and to pay the required fee.

flags: The reference note gives no due date. Under Rule 16 and 16A the return is generally due by 30 June each year, with data as on 31 March. Please verify.
The reference note's category list ends with 'etc'; Rule 2(1)(c) lists specific exempted receipts. Use the form's own categories.
The note that a director's DSC suffices for private companies is the reference note's; the form allows any authorised signatory.
private: The Director's digital signature is enough. There is no need for a Manager, CEO or CFO signature unless the company has one.

title: Transferring unclaimed dividend to the IEPF
law: Sections 124 and 125; Rules 5, 6 and 7 of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016
summary: Shows how a company finds dividend unclaimed for seven years, warns shareholders, moves the money to the IEPF and files the return.
when: When dividend has stayed in the unpaid dividend account for seven years.
applies: Companies that have declared dividend (listed and unlisted)

steps.d: Look at the Unpaid Dividend Account for amounts unpaid or unclaimed for seven consecutive years from when they were due. Example: a dividend declared on 15.09.2016 became due on or before 15.10.2016; if unclaimed until 15.10.2023 it must go to the IEPF.
Prepare a year-wise statement with name, last known address, folio or DP ID and client ID, and amount.
Send individual reminders by post or email telling them the amount will move to the IEPF.
steps.time: At least 3 months before the due date

steps.d: Place the statement before the board or a committee for noting, and pass a resolution authorising the transfer.
Fill in the IEPF-1 Excel template from the MCA website with dividend and shareholder details.
Transfer the dividend, with the related shares, to the IEPF Authority's bank account by online banking or NEFT. Example: for a due date of 15.10.2023, transfer by 14.11.2023.
steps.time: Within 30 days of the due date

steps.d: File e-form IEPF-1, attaching the challan or UTR, the certified statement of unclaimed dividend and the board resolution.
Mark the register of members and the dividend register 'Transferred to IEPF'.
Upload details of shareholders and amounts transferred on the website, searchable for at least 7 years.
Keep supporting documents safe, as they may be needed when shareholders claim refunds.

forms.purpose: Statement of amounts credited to the IEPF

checklist: Money transferred before the due date
IEPF-1 filed with challan and statement

meetings.title: Board meeting to note the unclaimed dividend and authorise transfer to the IEPF
meetings.notice_days: At least 7 days (shorter if the articles and Secretarial Standard 1 allow it)

resolutions.title: Transfer of unclaimed dividend to the IEPF
resolutions.text: RESOLVED THAT the statement of unclaimed dividend for the financial year [year], amounting to Rs. [amount], which has remained unpaid or unclaimed for seven years, as placed before the Board, be noted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT, as required by Section 124 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the IEPF Rules, the amount, together with the related shares, be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund by [date], and Form IEPF-1 be filed with the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name of director / company secretary] be authorised to do all things needed.

docs.title: Reminder to shareholders
paras: Dear Shareholder, our records show that dividend of Rs. [amount] for the year [year] on your [number] shares in {co} (folio / DP ID-Client ID [number]) has not been claimed.

Under Section 124 of the Companies Act, 2013, dividend unclaimed for seven consecutive years, and the related shares, must move to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. If you do not claim by [date], we will transfer them. Please write to [name and address of company] with your details to claim.

docs.title: Notice in newspapers
paras: NOTICE: {co} gives notice to shareholders whose dividend for the year [year] remains unclaimed. The dividend and the related shares will be transferred to the IEPF after [date]. Details of such shareholders are on our website at [website]. Please claim before that date.

flags: The reference note counts seven years from the date the dividend became due. Section 124(5) counts seven years from the date of transfer to the unpaid dividend account.

The reference note says shares move with the dividend through bank transfer. Shares go to the IEPF demat account, with a separate form (IEPF-4 for shares under Rule 6); the reference note does not name it.
The statutory 30-day period after the seven years should be checked against Section 124(5) and (6).
Rule 6 also asks for a newspaper notice before the transfer; the reference note mentions only individual reminders.
The reference note says private companies may be exempt from public notice and website disclosure. Sections 124 and 125 apply to all companies; check any exemption for private companies.
private: Public notice and website disclosure may not apply to certain private companies, unless they are treated as public or have public shareholders.

title: Updating a director's details on the DIN record
law: Section 153; Rule 12 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
summary: Explains how a director with an approved DIN tells the MCA about changed personal details using Form DIR-6 or DIR-3 KYC.
when: When a director's name, address, photograph, nationality, date of birth or other DIN details change.

steps.d: A director with an approved DIN files Form DIR-6 to tell the MCA of changes.
Tell the MCA of the change.
The director also tells each company in which he or she is a director.
Name, photograph, father's name, nationality, date of birth, gender, PAN, passport, Aadhaar or driving licence number, and present and permanent residential address.

Scan and attach proof of the change; proof of identity (PAN is mandatory for Indian nationals; a passport, apostilled, for foreign nationals); and proof of residence such as a bank statement, electricity, telephone or utility bill. Documents must be self-certified, and for foreign nationals notarised or apostilled. Aadhaar is not accepted as identity proof.
To change a personal mobile number or email, use DIR-3 KYC only. If KYC is already done in the financial year, you can update by filing DIR-3 KYC and paying Rs. 500.
steps.time: Fee of Rs. 500 if KYC is already done in the year

steps.d: A company secretary, chartered accountant or cost accountant in practice must certify DIR-6 or DIR-3 KYC digitally. It is wise for the professional to sign and stamp the attachments too.
Update the register of directors and key managerial personnel and the register of members as needed.

forms.purpose: Intimation of change in director's particulars
KYC of director, including change of mobile or email
forms.deadline: As needed; Rs. 500 if KYC is already done in the year

docs.title: Director's intimation of change of particulars
paras: To the Board of Directors, {co}.

I, [name], holding DIN [number], inform you that my [name / address / other particulars] changed on [date] from [old details] to [new details]. I have filed Form DIR-6 with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs on [date], SRN [number].
Please update the register of directors and key managerial personnel. Signed: [name], [date].

flags: The reference note says the form must be certified by 'a Company Secretary or a Chartered Accountant and a Cost Accountant'. It should read 'or'. Please verify.
The DIN rules now sit in Rule 12 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014; the reference note cites the Incorporation Rules. Please verify.
The list of changeable details repeats residential address; the reference note's mix of the two address items is unclear.
The Rs. 500 fee and the 30-day time limit should be checked against the current MCA fee schedule.

title: Giving a loan, guarantee or security where a director is interested (Section 185)
law: Section 185; Rule 10 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
summary: Shows how a company can give a loan, guarantee or security to a person in whom a director is interested, with board approval and a special resolution.
when: When a company plans a loan, guarantee or security to an entity in which its director is interested, and Section 185(2) allows it.
applies: All companies; some private companies are exempt

steps.d: Section 185(1) restricts loans (including book debts), guarantees or security to any director of the company or its holding company, a partner or relative of such a director, or a firm in which the director or relative is a partner. Section 185(2) allows them to persons in whom directors are interested, with a special resolution and certain conditions.
Consider the proposal, and approve the draft notice of the general meeting with the explanatory statement for a special resolution.
Include full particulars of the loan, guarantee or security; the purpose; confirmation that the borrower will use the funds for its principal business; and other relevant facts.
Send the notice with the Section 102 statement to the members.
steps.time: As for a general meeting (21 clear days, or shorter notice with consent)

steps.d: Pass the special resolution.
File it with the Registrar.
Show the transaction in the financial statements under the applicable accounting standard, and in the board's report.
Make sure the borrower uses the loan for its principal business only.
Record the loan, guarantee or security in the register kept for it.
Monitor the terms of the loan, guarantee or security from time to time.

[amount] to [name of borrower], at interest of [rate] per cent, repayable in [period], to be used by the borrower for its principal business activities. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the Board be authorised to do all things needed to give effect to this resolution.

[Name of director] is interested in this resolution because [reason]. No other director or key managerial personnel is interested.

flags: Section 185(1) is a prohibition and Section 185(2) is the permitted route; the reference note title says 'granting of loans to director', which is the part the Act forbids. Only the Section 185(2) route is covered by these steps.

Check that the interest rate is not below the prevailing yield of the one-year, three-year, five-year or ten-year Government security, as required for these transactions, which the reference note does not say.
The private company exemption in the reference note is cited from an MCA notification; check the current notification text, as conditions may differ.
The reference note calls the 'register maintained' without a form number; MBP-2 is the usual register for Section 186. Check.
Section 185 has other exceptions (ordinary course of business at a prescribed interest rate, holding to wholly owned subsidiary) listed in the reference note; check the interest rate condition.

title: Making loans, guarantees and investments in other companies (Section 186)
law: Sections 179(3)(e) and (f), and 186; Rules 11 and 12 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules, 2014
summary: Sets out the approvals for an inter-corporate loan, guarantee, security or investment, within or above the limit.
when: When a company lends to, guarantees for, or invests in another body corporate.
applies: All companies; some transactions are exempt under Section 186(3) and 186(11)

steps.d: Decide whether it is a loan, guarantee, security or investment. The total may not exceed 60% of paid-up capital, free reserves and securities premium, or 100% of free reserves and securities premium, whichever is more. Count earlier loans, guarantees, security and investments.
Hold the audit committee meeting if applicable, then a board meeting to approve the loan or investment.
steps.time: At least 7 days notice, or shorter notice

steps.d: After the board resolution, file it with the Registrar as Section 179(3) requires.
If the other party is outside India, consider FEMA rules.
Hold the audit committee meeting if applicable, then a board meeting to approve the loan or investment, and the notice and explanatory statement for a general meeting seeking a special resolution.
steps.time: At least 7 days notice, or shorter notice

steps.t: Above limits: file the board resolution
steps.d: File the board's approval.
Send the notice and the Section 102 statement with full particulars of the loan, guarantee or security, the purpose and other relevant facts.
Pass a special resolution. After that the company can enter the transaction.
File it with the Registrar.
Disclose the transaction in the financial statements under the right accounting standard and in the board's report. Make sure the borrower uses the loan for its principal business only.
Record loans, security and investments, with the board and shareholder approvals.
Entities and transactions prescribed in Section 186(3) and 186(11) are exempt.

flags: The reference note says MGT-14 must be filed after the board resolution under Section 179(3). Check it against Rule 24 of the Management Rules and the current exemptions.

Section 186(5) needs a board resolution with the unanimous consent of all directors present, and prior approval of a public financial institution where a term loan is outstanding. The reference note omits both.
Section 186(7) sets the minimum interest rate (not lower than the prevailing yield of Government securities of 1, 3, 5 or 10 year tenure). The reference note omits it.
The two-layer limit on investment companies is not mentioned in the reference note.
The reference note says private companies need not file MGT-14. A special resolution under Section 186(3) must still be filed; check the notification for any exemption.
private: A private company need not file Form MGT-14 for this resolution.
